body.statement:
On a joint probability space carrying the observed sample and \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\), suppose there is a deterministic sequence \(a_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left|
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1), \tag{7}
\]
and, on defining
\[
 R_n=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
       |\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_n(a)=
 \left\{k\in\mathcal K_n:
 Q_{n,k}(G_n)\le
 \min_{j\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,j}(G_n)+2a
 \right\},
\]
\[
 D_n(a)=\max_{k,l\in\mathcal M_n(a)}d_n(k,l),
\]
one has
\[
 \mathbb P_n(R_n\le a_n)\to1,
 \qquad
 D_n(a_n)\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{8}
\]
Then the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the law of
\(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\) and the law of
\(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)}\) tends to zero.  This is a conditional transfer result only: it does not assert that (7)--(8) hold for the generated fixed-cardinality prefix estimator.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(J_n=J_n(G_n)\).  On the event \(\{R_n\le a_n\}\), optimality of \(\widehat k_n\) for \(\widehat C_n\) and of \(J_n\) for \(Q_n(G_n)\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{n,\widehat k_n}(G_n)
 &\le \widehat C_{n,\widehat k_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &\le \widehat C_{n,J_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(\widehat k_n\)},\\
 &\le Q_{n,J_n}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &=\min_{j\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,j}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(J_n\)}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Thus \(\widehat k_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\); also \(J_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\) directly from the definition of that set.  Consequently,
\[
 d_n(\widehat k_n,J_n)\le D_n(a_n) \tag{10}
\]
on \(\{R_n\le a_n\}\).

For deterministic \(k,l\in\mathcal K_n\), the definition of \(d_n\) yields
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,l}|\le d_n(k,l),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l})
 \le d_n(k,l)^2. \tag{11}
\]
The second inequality remains valid when \(\Gamma_n\) is singular.  Let \(m_n=|\mathcal K_n|\).  If \(d_n(k,l)\le r\) for \(r>0\), the centered Gaussian variable \(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}\) has variance at most \(r^2\).  Its moment-generating function is therefore bounded by \(\exp(t^2r^2/2)\).  For \(u>0\), Markov's inequality gives the upper-tail bound \(\exp\{-tu+t^2r^2/2\}\); minimizing over \(t>0\) at \(t=u/r^2\), and applying the same argument to the lower tail, gives
\[
 \mathbb P\{|G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}|>u\}
 \le 2\exp\{-u^2/(2r^2)\}. \tag{12}
\]
There are at most \(m_n^2\) ordered pairs.  By (11), (12), and the union bound, for every \(x>0\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb P\Bigg[
 \max_{\substack{k,l\in\mathcal K_n\\d_n(k,l)\le r}}
 |(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})-(\beta_{n,l}+G_{n,l})|\\
 >r+r\sqrt{2\{\log(2m_n^2)+x\}}
 \Bigg]\le e^{-x}. 
 \end{split} \tag{13}
\]

Let \(L_n=\log(em_n)\).  The second condition in (8) says that
\(D_n(a_n)\sqrt{L_n}=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\).  Hence there exists a deterministic sequence \(c_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)\sqrt{L_n}>c_n\}\to0. \tag{14}
\]
For completeness, choose successively deterministic thresholds \(c_n\) decreasing to zero along indices after which the probability of exceeding the current threshold is at most that threshold; this diagonal construction proves (14) directly from convergence in probability.  Set \(r_n=c_n/\sqrt{L_n}\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)>r_n\}\to0,
 \qquad
 r_n\sqrt{L_n}=c_n\to0. \tag{15}
\]
Apply (13) with \(r=r_n\).  Since \(\log(2m_n^2)\le 2L_n+\log2\), equations (10), (13), and (15), together with \(\mathbb P_n(R_n\le a_n)\to1\), imply
\[
 (\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 -(\beta_{n,J_n}+G_{n,J_n})=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{16}
\]

Evaluating the maximum in (7) at the data-dependent index \(\widehat k_n\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{17}
\]
Combining (16) and (17),
\[
 \Delta_n:=
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{18}
\]
For every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 \left|E f(X_n)-E f(Y_n)\right|
 \le E\min\{2,|\Delta_n|\}, \tag{19}
\]
where \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\) are the two variables in (18).  For every \(u>0\), the right side of (19) is at most
\[
 u+2\mathbb P_n(|\Delta_n|>u),
\]
which tends to at most \(u\) by (18), and then to zero as \(u\downarrow0\).  Taking the supremum over the bounded-Lipschitz class proves the asserted convergence of laws.
body.justification: This lemma preserves the valid selection-transfer argument without asserting that its coupling and stability hypotheses follow from the current generated-ranking class.
body.gap: The unresolved mathematical work lies in establishing the lemma's hypotheses for the rank-corrected process, not in the transfer inequality itself.
body.consumer: It will convert a future primitive rank-corrected process theorem into the corresponding selected-estimator bounded-Lipschitz law.
